about: Temporary credit extension with a payment commitment (16 Nov 2026, the user's strict instruction): a separate workflow beside - never instead of - order approval (credit_commitment.json), credit periods (credit_period_request.json), credit conditions (credit_condition.json) and the credit sync. A rep (or the team's manager) asks for one on an order that takes a customer past their SAP credit limit. The manager may approve a temporary additional credit amount, within the manager's configured authority, with a payment commitment of at most 10 calendar days, and push it to SAP in the same step; the GM is not needed for that. The SAP job raises the customer's SAP CreditLimit by the amount, watches confirmed SAP payments from the approval date to the commitment date, and puts the original limit back when the commitment is paid or the date has passed. Unpaid by the date: 'Payment Commitment Overdue', with the GM, who approves a new extension (and pushes it) or rejects. Implemented by the manna_credit_extension Server Script (app/server/credit_extension.py, enforced), the phone (app/lib/core/credit_extension.dart), the dashboard (client/src/domain/creditExtension.ts) and the SAP job (sap-credit-sync/Sync-CreditExtensions.ps1); all four test against this file. 17 Nov 2026 added the manager cap (routing, manager_window: server and both apps), per-manager authority (authority: the server, which sends the apps the figure), and the daily watchdog with its late check (watchdog, late_check: the manna_credit_extension_watch Server Script and the main script, app/server/credit_extension_watch.py).

rules.eligible: An order still waiting for approval whose customer's outstanding plus the order total goes past a credit limit that is set - credit.json's over-limit test. The excess is outstanding + order - limit.
rules.routing: A new request goes to the Manager, unless the customer has ever missed a commitment, already has an extension that is not finished, or has had the manager's cap of extensions in the window - then to the GM. No unlimited manager extensions.
rules.manager_cap: 17 Nov 2026, the user's default: at most manager_cap_count manager-approved extensions per customer in any manager_cap_days calendar days (Manna Credit Extension Settings, default 2 in 90). An extension counts from the day the manager approved it, whatever became of it after - paid, overdue, renewed. GM approvals do not count. A cap of 0 sends every request to the GM. Checked when the request is made AND when the manager approves, so a request made before the cap filled cannot slip past it.
rules.authority: 17 Nov 2026: the manager's authority is their own row in Manna Credit Extension Settings.authorities (manager, max_amount), else the settings' manager_max_amount for every manager. A row of 0 means that manager has none, even when the default is set. Decided by the Server Script; the apps show the figure it sends.
rules.watchdog: 17 Nov 2026: the escalation must not depend on the office server's SAP job running. A daily Server Script (manna_credit_extension_watch) takes every 'Active' extension whose commitment date is before today to 'Payment Commitment Overdue', escalates it to the GM and notifies the manager and the GM, marked 'not yet checked against SAP' (overdue_unchecked) and with the SAP restore pending. It does NOT mark the commitment missed: only SAP's payments can say that. The commitment day itself belongs to the customer. Errs toward escalating: a GM who looks at one that turns out paid has lost a minute; a missed commitment nobody escalated is the failure the user named.
rules.late_check: When the SAP job later counts the payments of an unchecked overdue extension: paid in full by the commitment date -> 'Paid' if it is still waiting on the GM (the GM and manager are told), or left as the GM decided if the GM already renewed or rejected it; not paid -> the commitment is missed, and the status stays. Either way it is now checked. The escalation's notifications were sent when it was escalated and are not sent again.
rules.manager_approval: Amount > 0, at most the manager's authority (Manna Credit Extension Settings.manager_max_amount; 0 or unset means the manager has none and must send it to the GM), commitment date from the approval day to 10 calendar days after it, reason and remarks both required. Approving pushes to SAP in the same step.
rules.gm_approval: Amount > 0, a commitment date from today on, remarks required. From 'Payment Commitment Overdue' the GM's approval makes a NEW extension record linked to the overdue one, which becomes 'Renewed by GM'; no record is ever overwritten.
rules.reject: Remarks required. A rejected request is never sent to SAP.
rules.sap_raise: Reads the SAP limit; the original is the one saved at the first push, else SAP's now. Refused if SAP's limit is 0 (no figure), if another extension of the customer is still raised in SAP, or if SAP's limit is neither the original nor original + amount (somebody changed it). Original + amount already = already done.
rules.commitment_limit: SAP refuses a credit limit above the customer's commitment limit (MaxCommitment, OCRD.DebtLine: 'Commitment limit must be greater than credit limit', TEST_MANNA_TREADS 16 Nov 2026), and every customer with a limit there has the two equal. So the raise lifts the commitment limit to at least the new credit limit in the same write, and the restore puts both back - the user's choice, 16 Nov 2026. Its original is saved and checked like the credit limit's: a commitment limit somebody changed is never overwritten.
rules.payments: Incoming payments in SAP for the customer, dated from the approval date to the commitment date, not cancelled, not a draft (Proforma): CashSum + TransferSum + cheques + cards + bills of exchange. Each counted once, by DocEntry.
rules.outcome: Paid when payments reach the amount, at any time up to the commitment date. Unpaid or partly paid after the commitment date: 'Payment Commitment Overdue', escalated to the GM once, the manager and GM notified once.
rules.sap_restore: After Paid or Overdue: SAP's limit and commitment limit back to their originals - only if SAP still holds what the raise wrote. Both already the originals: restored. Anything else: 'Needs Review', never overwritten.
